test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 05
subject: general
question: The term “Phesgo,” recently seen in the news, is related to:

options.text: A single-dose injectable formulation for treating breast cancer.
A diagnostic imaging technique used in early breast cancer detection.
A robotic surgical device for tumor excision.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Phesgo is an injection-based breast cancer treatment that combines trastuzumab and pertuzumab, offering a faster, simpler, and equally effective alternative to traditional intravenous infusions for HER2-positive breast cancer patients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Phesgo delivers two key monoclonal antibodies — trastuzumab and pertuzumab — through subcutaneous (under-the-skin) injection rather than lengthy IV infusions. Hence, it reduces hospital time and improves patient comfort.
 
• Studies confirm that Phesgo is as safe and effective as IV therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer.
 
• It is already used in major hospitals in India, though access remains uneven due to cost and system constraints. Hence, it represents progress in bridging treatment gaps in India’s oncology care.
 
• The innovation aligns with global trends toward simplified, evidence-based oncology treatments. **Hence, Option A is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• HER2-positive breast cancer accounts for about **20–25% of all breast cancer cases**.
 
• The subcutaneous delivery of drugs like **Phesgo** significantly reduces hospital time — from **2.5 hours to about 5–8 minutes per session**.
 
• Broader adoption of such treatments could improve access and reduce healthcare costs, especially in resource-constrained systems.
